pros: Guaranteed O(n log n) time complexity in all cases
Stable sort: preserves relative order of equal elements
Predictable performance regardless of input distribution
Excellent for sorting linked lists (O(1) extra space on lists)
Natural fit for external sorting (data larger than RAM)
Fewer comparisons than Quick Sort (n log n vs 1.39 n log n)
Can count inversions during merge (useful for array analysis)
Deterministic and easy to analyze mathematically
Can be optimized for partially sorted data (natural merge sort)
cons: Extra memory allocation can be expensive for large n
Slower than Quick Sort in practice due to copying overhead
Performs O(n log n) even on already-sorted input (basic version)
Recursive implementation uses O(log n) stack space
Constant factor higher than Quick Sort's average case
Not cache-optimal for very large arrays (memory bandwidth limited)
Overhead of temporary array allocation and copying
Merging step requires careful bounds checking or sentinels
Poor performance on small arrays (switching to insertion sort helps)
Non-adaptive basic version wastes effort on sorted subsequences
Implementation complexity with correct index management
